staged_source_snapshot.description: Stage 01 reproduced against this staged vulnerable checkout. Sample metadata names `598b330050a94bbe6bdc804d969d216f351261a0`, but the local staged source is an earlier still-vulnerable revision whose line map matches the saved crash (`uncompressgzipped:565`, `uncompressbuf:1032`, `file_zmagic:311`).

bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42516204 (file): Heap-buffer-overflow READ 1 found by fuzz target magic_fuzzer [asan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42516204
bug_description.original_source: ARVO-Meta / OSS-Fuzz report / staged vulnerable workspace `git rev-parse HEAD`
bug_description.normalized: Stage 01 reproduced `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 1` in `uncompressgzipped()` from the staged vulnerable checkout `5f957469b734366c8d4cbd050609ba4cc3a5c47c`. The exact witness is the 2-byte file `1f 8b`: `file_zmagic()` only requires those two bytes to match the gzip signature at `compr[2]`, then copies `nbytes = 2` into `nsz` and calls `uncompressbuf(..., i = 2, buf, &nsz)`. `uncompressbuf()` forwards that same short buffer to `uncompressgzipped()`'s built-in gzip path. In the vulnerable source, `uncompressgzipped()` immediately evaluates `old[3]` to materialize `flg` even though `*n == 2`; the patch fixes this exact obligation by adding `if (*n < 4) goto err;` before the read. The saved ASan trace reports the resulting one-byte read past the 2-byte heap testcase buffer at `src/compress.c:565` with stack `uncompressgzipped -> uncompressbuf -> file_zmagic -> file_buffer -> magic_buffer`.

source.description: First project-side parse of the attacker bytes on the witnessed path. At compressor-table index `i = 2`, this comparison recognizes the 2-byte witness as gzip input and selects the decompressor path that later overreads the header.
source.value_from: The staged testcase `gt_results/arvo_42516204/poc` is exactly 2 bytes long (sha256 `ee98dc6af27a9f1c8cc4aaa2fd05b5f6e7c98f51390253a5263b0d096c3510fe`) and contains only `0x1f 0x8b`. In `file_zmagic()`, the earlier minimum-length check at line 289 only requires `nbytes >= 2` for `compr[2]`, so this `memcmp` is reached and returns true on the witness.

sink.description: ASan crash site. The function reads `old[3]` from a 2-byte heap buffer while parsing a truncated gzip header.
sink.note: The saved trace says the accessed address is 1 byte to the right of the 2-byte testcase region and attributes the read to `uncompressgzipped /src/file/src/compress.c:565:22`.

root_cause.description: Missing precondition check: `uncompressgzipped()` reads the fourth gzip-header byte without first ensuring that `*n >= 4`.
root_cause.note: The staged patch inserts `if (*n < 4) goto err;` immediately before this access. On the witnessed path, `file_zmagic()` propagated `nbytes = 2` into `*n`, so the fixed guard would reject the buffer instead of reading past it.

parser_admitted.description: With `nbytes == 2`, the witness satisfies the gzip table entry's 2-byte minimum at line 289 and matches `compr[2]`'s magic bytes here, so `file_zmagic()` continues into `uncompressbuf()` instead of rejecting the buffer as too short or non-gzip.

tainted_value_origin.description: This assignment copies the attacker-controlled 2-byte input length into the exact `size_t` later observed as `*n` inside `uncompressgzipped()`.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: Step 0 materializes `nbytes = b->flen = 2` for the staged witness, and this statement preserves that exact short length in `nsz` before passing `&nsz` into the decompressor chain.

coarse_trace.summary: The compression probe materializes the 2-byte testcase buffer, the bytes `0x1f 0x8b` match `compr[2]`'s gzip signature, and `file_zmagic()` propagates `nbytes = 2` into `nsz` before calling `uncompressbuf()`.
Method `2` (`METH_FROZEN`, the gzip entry) forwards the same `old` pointer and short length reference into `uncompressgzipped()` without any additional header-length validation.
The gzip helper lacks the required `*n < 4` rejection before materializing `flg` from `old[3]`, so the 2-byte witness causes the saved heap-buffer-overflow read at line 565.

fine_trace.code:
const unsigned char *buf = CAST(const unsigned char *, b->fbuf);
size_t nbytes = b->flen;
fine_trace.note: The compression detector materializes the testcase buffer pointer and its length from `struct buffer b`. For the staged witness, `buf` points at the 2-byte heap region `1f 8b` and `nbytes = 2`, which is enough to pass the later `nbytes < abs(compr[i].maglen)` check for the gzip table entry because `compr[2].maglen == 2`.

At compressor-table index `i = 2` (the gzip entry), `memcmp()` reads the two attacker bytes and sets `zm = 1` because they exactly match `0x1f 0x8b`. That is the first project-side parse of the witness bytes and it selects the gzip-specific path.

Because the `if (!zm) continue;` branch is not taken after step 1, `file_zmagic()` copies `nbytes` into `nsz` and passes the same `buf` pointer plus `&nsz` to `uncompressbuf()`. For the witness this creates the exact decompressor arguments `old = buf` and `*n = 2`.

With call argument `i = 2`, `method` enters the `METH_FROZEN` switch arm and `uncompressbuf()` forwards the same `old` pointer and `n` reference to `uncompressgzipped()` without validating that the gzip header is at least 4 bytes long.

This helper starts parsing the gzip header with no precheck that the input is long enough for `old[3]`. On the witnessed path `*n` is still 2, but vulnerable source has no `if (*n < 4) goto err;` before the flags-byte access; the staged patch adds exactly that missing guard here.

ASan attributes the crash to this load: the saved trace reports a `READ of size 1` on an address `1 byte to the right of 2-byte region [0x602000000110,0x602000000112)` and names `uncompressgzipped /src/file/src/compress.c:565:22` as frame 0.

sanitizer_ground_truth.source: staged `sanitizer_trace.txt`, `default_crash_trace.txt`, and `reproduction_report.json`; Stage 02 did not run fixed-version dynamic validation

poc.trigger: Stage 01's saved vulnerable run executed `PYTHONPATH=gt_generation python3 -m gt_toolkit arvo-workspace --result-dir /mnt/datastore/gt_generation/gt_results/arvo_42516204 run --version vulnerable --expect crash`, which fed `gt_results/arvo_42516204/poc` to `/out/magic_fuzzer` and reproduced `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 1` in `uncompressgzipped()`.

format.name: Exact 2-byte gzip magic prefix
format.contract: Exactly the staged 2-byte witness stored in `gt_results/arvo_42516204/poc` (sha256 `ee98dc6af27a9f1c8cc4aaa2fd05b5f6e7c98f51390253a5263b0d096c3510fe`), whose bytes are only `0x1f 0x8b`. Those two bytes must be enough for `file_zmagic()` to satisfy its `nbytes >= abs(compr[2].maglen)` precheck and make `memcmp()` match the gzip table entry `compr[2]`. The same witness must then keep `nbytes = 2` through `nsz = nbytes` and `uncompressbuf(..., i = 2, ..., &nsz)`, so `uncompressgzipped()` is entered with `*n == 2` and immediately reads `old[3]` before any `if (*n < 4) goto err;` rejection.
